The hook SLOT is right and the turn gate matches, but CardCmd.DiscardAndDraw does two things the sim's inline loop does not: it routes each discard through CardPileCmd.Add (G2) and, after the draw, it AUTO-PLAYS every discarded card that was Sly this turn (G1). guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): CardCmd.DiscardAndDraw auto-plays every discarded card that `IsSlyThisTurn`, AFTER the draw (CardCmd.cs:186-204); the sim's loop has no Sly concept
guards.issue: MECHANISM: DiscardAndDraw collects `if (card.IsSlyThisTurn) slyCards.Add(card)` while discarding (CardCmd.cs:188-191), draws, and then `foreach (CardModel item in slyCards) await AutoPlay(choiceContext, item, null, AutoPlayType.SlyDiscard)` (CardCmd.cs:201-204). So mulliganing a Sly card with Gambling Chip PLAYS it for free on turn 1. gambling_chip.py:32-36 moves cards to the discard pile and draws, with no Sly branch anywhere. DORMANT, and the concrete unported thing is named: Sly does not exist in the sim at all -- executed `git grep -in 'is_sly\|CardKeyword.Sly' -- sts2_rl` returns ZERO hits (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`). Porting the Sly keyword (CardKeyword.Sly / CardCmd.ApplySingleTurnSly, CardCmd.cs:698-701) makes it live immediately, and it would land in the strongest possible direction: a free turn-1 card play the sim silently drops. Note the fix belongs in a shared discard helper, not in this relic -- the sim has no DiscardCmd at all (grep `class DiscardCmd` over cmds.py returns nothing), so every discard site would need it.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): each discard goes through `CardPileCmd.Add(card, discardPile)` in C# (CardCmd.cs:192) where the sim mutates the two lists directly (gambling_chip.py:33-34)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardPileCmd.Add runs the game's pile-change machinery -- Hook.ShouldAddToDeck / Hook.ModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck for deck adds, and Hook.AfterCardChangedPiles(+Late) generally -- plus `discardPile.InvokeContentsChanged()` after the loop. The sim has no card-changed-piles hook to dispatch, so the raw list mutation is all there is. DORMANT: `after_card_added_to_deck` is the sim's only pile-change hook and it is scoped to the run DECK (relics/base.py:208-210), not to combat piles; the one C# hook that fires on a combat pile change and has ported implementers is AfterCardChangedPiles(Late), whose absence is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json's own step-28 phase/dispatch finding rather than this relic's. Porting an AfterCardChangedPiles listener (SoulFysh.cs's AfterCardChangedPilesLate is the ported-monster example) makes it live. Worth recording for the fixer: gambling_chip.py:33-35 appends to the discard pile BEFORE firing on_card_discarded, which is the C# order (Add then Hook.AfterCardDiscarded), whereas player.discard_hand (player.py:188-196) fires the hook FIRST -- the two sim discard sites disagree with each other and this one is the correct one.

guards.what: G3: `CardSelectorPrefs(prompt, 0, 999999999)` -- minimum ZERO -- so the game lets the player keep the whole hand; the sim's default selector always discards `count` cards
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: 'discard nothing' is expressible. `gambling_chip` is now in sts2_rl/driver.py:87-89 SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES, whose comment cites GamblingChip.cs:12's `CardSelectorPrefs(prompt, 0, 999999999)` MinSelect-0 shape by name; RunDriver._card_selector therefore skips the `count >= len(remaining)` short-circuit (driver.py:263-266) and issues a real DecisionRequest whose legal_actions() appends the skip index, and sts2_rl/relics/gambling_chip.py:26-30 returns early when the selector returns an empty list. guards.what: N3: `CardCmd.DiscardAndDraw(ctx, list, list.Count)` draws exactly as many as were discarded, and the discards all happen BEFORE the draw
guards.rationale: gambling_chip.py:32-36 discards every chosen card in the loop and only then calls DrawCmd.draw(player, len(chosen)) -- same count, same order. This matters because the discarded cards must be in the discard pile before the draw so a reshuffle can pick them up, and DiscardAndDraw's own doc comment (CardCmd.cs:162-168) is explicit that only the SLY handling is deferred past the draw, not the discard itself. The `if list.Count != 0` / `if not chosen: return` early exits also match, which keeps a zero-card choice from burning a reshuffle.
